rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.7, 3.2, Table 2 - the authors developed a float-sensor/RF/microcontroller automated irrigation system and field-tested it in Kharif 2018-19 at the CIAE farm against a continuous-ponding control plot, measuring pump discharge with a water meter. Q2: Section 3.2 and Table 2 - the automated AWD system achieved total water savings of 36% over the continuous-ponding control, with irrigation water productivity 6.15 vs 3.06 kg/ha/mm and total water productivity 4.80 vs 2.63. Q7: Section 3.2 limitations paragraph - the system requires a reliable power source and the pump house must be within the 100 m RF range of the field sensor; Section 2.6 - the field must first be laser-levelled so irrigation water flows smoothly across it. Q8: Section 3.2 limitations paragraph and Conclusions - the system is designed only for rice under AWD, communication range limited to 100 m, larger fields would need multiple sensors/valves, and the study compares AWD vs continuous ponding focusing on system development and water saving rather than crop performance effects.
rows.notes: Technology matches (sensor-microcontroller-actuation smart irrigation). Caveat: the 36% water saving is for automated AWD versus manual continuous ponding, so the saving attributable to automation per se is confounded with the AWD regime, which the authors themselves acknowledge. Single plot pair, one season, one site, one cultivar; water saving measured by a single water meter (no triangulation). Water levels were monitored by the sensors but no field water-level, percolation or ponding-time data are reported as an intermediate variable, so Q4 is no. Yield is given with SD (4.8 <U+00B1> 0.189 vs 4.1 <U+00B1> 0.429 t/ha) but the water saving and water productivity figures carry no dispersion measure, so Q9 is no. The claimed range 11-42% is the review's synthesis; this study contributes a single 36% value.

notes: Full text available; some pages are duplicated/garbled by OCR overlap but content is readable. The study is a design-and-test paper with one field season and one treatment pair.
